issue.title: Disabled provider-qualified group member resolves to unselected model on another provider (group/pro -> commandcode)
issue.body:
# Disabled provider-qualified group member resolves to an unselected model on another provider

Magpie v0.1.1560 (revision `19253f67bca2310c32739a6eaac88546b3574dbc`, macOS arm64).

A configured group member `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` is reported by `magpie group show pro` as skipped because the `xiaomi` provider is off. However, live group requests resolve that member to `commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` and successfully invoke Command Code. The Command Code provider has only `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` selected.

## Relevant configuration

```json
{
  "providers": [
    {"id": "xiaomi", "models": ["mimo-v2.6-flash", "mimo-v2.6-pro"], "off": true},
    {"id": "commandcode", "models": ["deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"]},
    {"id": "commandcode-plan", "models": ["deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"], "hidden": true}
  ],
  "groups": [
    {
      "id": "pro",
      "members": ["zhipu/glm-5.3", "xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro", "codex/gpt-6.1-sol"],
      "routing": "order"
    }
  ]
}
```

The full Command Code catalog contains the vendor model ID `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`, but it is absent from the selected `models` list. Zhipu is paused by a time rule during the observed requests.

## Expected behavior

`xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` should remain bound to the configured `xiaomi` provider and be skipped while that provider is off, consistently with `magpie group show pro`. It should not silently acquire a different provider prefix.

If resolving a model ID across providers is intentional, explicit provider-qualified references must be distinguished from bare model IDs; selection and catalog semantics should be documented and applied consistently.

## Observed behavior

CLI output:

```text
2 xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro  not served: Xiaomi MiMo is off now, skipped
```

Sanitized first observed route:

```json
{
  "id": 1792985013193,
  "time": "2026-10-26T14:10:48.674174+08:00",
  "model": "group/pro",
  "group": {
    "id": "pro",
    "members": ["commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro", "codex/gpt-6.1-sol"]
  },
  "tries": [{"id": "commandcode", "model": "xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro", "status": 499}]
}
```

Subsequent records contain the same rewritten member and successful Command Code attempts with status 200 and `served: "xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro"`. Across the retained logs examined (2026-10-16 through 2026-10-26), there were 53 matching group requests, all on October 26, of which 52 had a successful matching attempt. These are request counts, not conversation counts. The configuration snapshot verifies the selection at investigation time; it does not establish historical selection state for every request.

## Source-level cause

The source at the installed revision confirms the resolution path:

1. [`membersOff`, group.go:885–886](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/19253f67bca2310c32739a6eaac88546b3574dbc/internal/provider/group.go#L885) resolves the stored group member through `resolveIn(entries, model)`.
2. [`resolveIn`, models.go:2654–2659](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/19253f67bca2310c32739a6eaac88546b3574dbc/internal/provider/models.go#L2654) splits the reference at the first slash and returns the named provider only when it is on. Finding an existing disabled provider does not terminate resolution.
3. It then compares the entire original string against bare `Entry.Model` values (2661–2664), followed by an explicit `// not exposed, but some provider lists it` lookup through `listedBy` (2666–2674). A unique provider listing the entire original string is accepted.
4. [`listedBy`, models.go:2680–2694](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/19253f67bca2310c32739a6eaac88546b3574dbc/internal/provider/models.go#L2680) indexes every enabled provider's `Available()` models, rather than its selected `models` list.

Thus an explicit reference to a disabled provider can be reinterpreted as a bare model ID and acquire another provider. The original `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` string exactly matches a Command Code catalog model. This explains both the provider substitution and why an unselected catalog model can be reached. Request tracing was not added, so the precise successful fallback branch (bare entry match versus unique full-catalog match) is not instrumented; the configuration and catalog support the latter.

The correction should preserve provider binding once a reference's prefix identifies an existing configured provider, even when it is disabled. Group member resolution should not reinterpret such a reference through another provider's catalog. Regression coverage should distinguish known-disabled provider prefixes, genuine bare upstream IDs containing slashes, and selected versus unselected models. Changing all unselected-model semantics globally would require a separate product decision because the resolver explicitly supports direct requests for unexposed models.

## Local workaround attempted, then reverted

For verification only, I temporarily disabled the two exact Command Code references with `magpie model disable commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro commandcode-plan/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`. After that setting persisted, new `group/pro` route snapshots no longer included the MiMo member. That workaround has since been reverted with `magpie model enable`; no local patch or persistent setting remains. No synthetic model calls were made for testing; counts come from live request logs.

comments.body:
Fixed on a fork branch: `fix/3698-prefix-off` (head `6d7c04d0`, on upstream `6afbe3f3`) — a member naming a provider that is off resolves nowhere, instead of re-binding to another provider.

**Root cause.** `internal/provider/models.go`'s `resolveIn`: the `provider/model` prefix branch requires `p.On() && !p.ServesNone()`, and on failure it fell through to the bare `e.Model == id` loop over `All()` — so `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` re-bound to commandcode's copy of that id.

**Change.** when the prefix names a provider that exists but isn't serving, the id does not resolve at all; an unknown prefix still falls through, so bare ids containing a slash (vendor ids) behave as before. Callers that report why a member isn't served (`membersOff`, group share, groupfast, `bare.go`) now say off instead of serving another provider's model — checked, `magpie group show` already words it that way.

**Verified.** Red: `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider/ -run TestPrefixOfAnOffProviderResolvesNowhere` → `models_test.go:325: xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro resolved to commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` and the group served the re-bound member
Green: `same command → `ok`; the gateway/cli/agent sibling suites that resolve models are unaffected` → `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider`

This is the ambiguity the report asks to resolve toward the prefix; a genuine bare id whose first segment happens to equal a provider id now resolves nowhere while that provider is off — worth a nod if you'd rather keep the fall-through for that case.

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` over round 26's branches: 70 packages ok, 5 red (edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`, gateway's five, plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, provider's synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials`, testenv `TestProgram`) — every one of them reproduces identically at base `6afbe3f3` in this environment (umask 0027), so none is from this change.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3698-prefix-off — no PR opened, this repo takes no external PRs; say the word if you'd rather have the patch inline here.

### Conclusion

I independently reproduced the bad rebinding on Windows/amd64 at `ed978e56` on 2026-11-02. The prefix-termination behavior proposed in the existing patch is correct: an explicitly named provider that is off or serves none resolves nowhere.

### Evidence

With the reported fixture, baseline `Resolve("xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro")` returned `commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`. With `resolveIn` terminating immediately after a configured-provider prefix match:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `xiaomi` off, `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` | unresolved |
| `xiaomi` on, the same id | `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` |
| Unknown prefix `xiaomi/...` before `xiaomi` exists | still resolves to the one provider listing the full slash id |
| Explicit `commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` | still resolves to Command Code |

The provider regression tests passed. Reverting the prefix branch to the old fall-through made the contract fail with the original `commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro` result. Re-restoring the change made it pass. `gofmt`, Windows/Linux vet, and Windows/Linux/macOS builds passed.

### Boundary

Unknown prefixes still fall through to bare-model and `listedBy` resolution, so genuine vendor ids containing slashes keep working. On-prefix behavior and the explicit `provider/model` escape are unchanged.

### Gap

Not tried: a real Xiaomi or Command Code account, and macOS execution. The full provider suite is interrupted here by the existing Windows-only `TestRestartSwitchedCodexAppReal` helper failure, which also happens at `ed978e56`.

### Action

This is consistent with the existing `fix/3698-prefix-off` result; no second branch is needed from me.

### Conclusion

Correction to my previous comment: I said no second branch was needed. That was wrong after the request for a complete end-to-end patch. A fork branch with the tested behavior is now published.

### Evidence

- Branch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/tree/codex/issue-3698-prefix
- Commit: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/b27bde464afc4914193c56c470f385418699436e
- Patch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/b27bde464afc4914193c56c470f385418699436e.patch
- Compare: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/compare/173b7e2742530dc6c9b7cd14f63cbf8eafc79f9c...codex/issue-3698-prefix
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider -run 'TestPrefixOfAnOffProviderResolvesNowhere$' -count=1`: pass
- `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, Windows/Linux `go vet`, Windows/Linux/macOS top-level builds: pass

This is an independent implementation of the same binding rule as skygunner's existing branch; the patches are interchangeable.

### Boundary

A configured provider prefix now terminates resolution whether the provider is on, off, or Select none. An unknown prefix still falls through for a genuine slash-bearing vendor id; the explicit `provider/model` escape remains unchanged.

### Gap

Not tried: real Xiaomi or Command Code accounts; macOS execution.

### Action

Cherry-pick `b27bde464`, or run:

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie.git codex/issue-3698-prefix
git cherry-pick b27bde464afc4914193c56c470f385418699436e
```

The issue remains open for your review.

### Conclusion

On 2026-11-10, the prefix-binding fix was refreshed against `40118730018fe48db225f13ff56b8ec2f1d75fa4` (`v0.1.3585`), because the earlier branch no longer applies cleanly to current `origin/main`. A configured provider prefix now terminates resolution even when that provider is off or set to Select none.

### Evidence

- Branch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/tree/codex/issue-3698-prefix-20261110
- Commit: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/86fe0a172
- Patch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/86fe0a172.patch
- Compare: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/compare/40118730018fe48db225f13ff56b8ec2f1d75fa4...codex/issue-3698-prefix-20261110

On clean `401187300`, the regression test failed with `off prefix resolved to "commandcode" "xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro"`. With the patch, the focused provider test passed:

```text
ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider 2.584s
```

The test also keeps the deliberate fall-through for an unknown prefix and covers `commandcode/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro`, group member filtering, and a Select none provider. `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, Windows/Linux `go vet`, and Windows/Linux/macOS top-level builds passed.

### Boundary

Only a prefix that names a configured provider terminates resolution. An unknown prefix still falls through for a genuine slash-bearing upstream model id. The explicit `provider/model` escape remains available.

### Gap

Not tried: real Xiaomi or Command Code accounts, macOS execution, and the full provider suite.

### Action

This is an independent implementation of the same binding rule as skygunner's existing branch; the implementations are interchangeable. Cherry-pick `86fe0a172`, or run:

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie.git codex/issue-3698-prefix-20261110
git cherry-pick 86fe0a172
```

No issue status change is requested.
